title: DOISST has 9-10% less Nino 3.4 amplitude than OI v2 after trend and step removal in 1982-2022
abstract: We tested whether mean-step removal also removes the ENSO amplitude difference between two SST source records used for AMIP forcing. We used verified monthly Nino 3.4 aggregates for 1982-2022. After calendar means, a linear trend and five input steps are removed, DOISST v2.1 has 8.7-9.6% less amplitude than OI SST v2. Three third-product instruments give gains of 0.904-0.913. All conditional intervals with 12, 24 and 48-month blocks are below one. Gains remain below one in both input eras and after three large El Nino episodes are removed. Symmetric variance ratios also show smaller DOISST amplitude against three complete references. A constant gain improves conditional held-out reconstruction, but quadratic and seasonal terms give no consistent added benefit. Warm-cold gain differences are uncertain. This extends the prior amplitude observation with noise, event and shape tests. It does not identify true SST amplitude, test final forcing files, or measure an atmosphere response. Shared input errors can violate the instrument assumption. Code, aggregate results, source hashes and a separate-scratch reproduction script are included.

display.caption: DOISST amplitude decrease relative to OI v2 after calendar, trend and five step terms are removed. Points use three third-product instruments. Lines show conditional 95% intervals from 24-month blocks with nuisance refits.
Reference-specific gains for the two SST sources. The third-product instrument test does not assume that one reference is exact.

citations.reason: Numerical input and prior report of smaller DOISST ENSO anomalies. We add third-product gain, direct source comparison, shape tests and conditional reconstruction.
AMIP prototype source context. We test regional source records, not its processed forcing fields.
